_comment: Transport and orbit (see Transport.cs): sail ships and laser stations, satellites, and the lift-to-orbit ladder. Missing values use the defaults in code.
_sailsComment: A sail ship's acceleration (its class's accelMmPerHour2) is what it gets in full sunlight at sunAu from the star. Sunlight falls with the square of the distance (capped at maxLight times); in a planet's or moon's shadow it is 0. A laser station of the side within laserRangeMm and in sight adds laserPush (in the same units: 1 = full sunlight at sunAu). A route is flown with the average push along it, and refused below minPush. Sails make no plume: a sailing fleet shows like a cold one.
_satellitesComment: Satellites: launched from a body the side holds to the orbit of any body, or to a planet's (or moon's) leading or trailing point, 60 degrees ahead of or behind it on its orbit. They fly there at speedMmPerHour. Sensor satellites see like a ship with sensorMm; relay satellites pass orders and reports round planets like a relay station. Each costs its Industry plus the lift of liftGoods goods from where it is launched. Enemies see one only from seenMm times their sensors (a tiny, cold target); an armed enemy fleet within killRangeMm that sees it shoots it down (killPerHour chance an hour). A side may have maxPerSide at once. Lost ones stay listed for keepLostDays.

kinds.name: Sensor satellite
kinds.effect: Watches space round it like a picket ship: sees burning fleets far off, cold ones only close

kinds.name: Relay satellite
kinds.effect: Passes orders and reports round planets that block them, like a relay station, from wherever it sits

_liftComment: The lift to orbit: every good a freighter, tanker or supply ship loads at a body, and every satellite launched from it, costs industryPerGood Industry times the body's gravity well (its mass over its radius, 1 for an Earth-sized world drawn refRadiusMm across; asteroids and small moons are almost free; at most maxWell). The ladder cuts it: a working mass driver on the body (massDriver), a skyhook over it, or a space elevator down to it (their stations' liftCut); the best one counts.
